build_readiness._comment: Complete this BEFORE dispatching a signed release workflow. Nothing here depends on the signed candidate existing.
build_readiness.credential_owner_apple: REPLACE — owner of the Apple signing credentials

submission_readiness._comment: Complete this AFTER the signed candidate has been distributed to Play Internal Testing / TestFlight and qualified on a physical device. Do not fill it in ahead of time. Each *_candidate block identifies ONE exact signed candidate; get its values from `scripts/generate_release_manifest.sh checksum <release-manifest.json>` or from the signed workflow's run log.
submission_readiness.release_approver: REPLACE — the person who approved this production release

android_candidate._comment: The exact signed Android candidate that was installed and tested. A build number alone does not identify a candidate.

device_qualification.outcome: REPLACE — pass only if the candidate actually passed

ios_candidate._comment: The exact signed iOS candidate that was installed from TestFlight and tested. This is a different workflow run from the Android one, with its own manifest.

device_qualification.outcome: REPLACE — pass only if the candidate actually passed

notes: Android build readiness only, recorded on behalf of the Release Operator so the signed Android workflow can be dispatched for 0.0.33. The Data Safety answers were re-checked against this version's new event-link share path: sharing a public-calendar event POSTs only {calendarUrl, uid, occurrenceId} to the unauthenticated CalEmbed endpoint, with no account, session, event content or device identifier, so no new collected data type is introduced over 0.0.32. The Apple fields (credential owner, certificate and provisioning-profile expiry, iOS listing and App Privacy checks) are deliberately left unfilled — no iOS release of 0.0.33 has been prepared, so an iOS signed build fails closed until the Credential Owner — Apple completes them. submission_readiness is untouched: it is completed only after the signed candidate exists and has been qualified on a physical device.
